rationale: Ground truth here is nearly devoid of substantive content (empty human reviews, and inline comments are just procedural 'do not change this'/'PTAL'/'LGTM' on files/lines largely outside or barely touching the diff), so recall differences are small — both candidates show awareness of the MUSA/quickstart revert context (X via a PR-body quote, Y via an explicit byte-identical verification against the merge-base and a cited revert commit), giving Y a slight edge. On their own findings, both are well-grounded in the diff and repo state with no obvious fabrication, but Y is far more thorough (7 solidly cross-referenced comments vs X's 2) and consistently more actionable, offering concrete replacement text, verification commands, and precise reasoning (e.g., the RC-vs-stable branch pin inconsistency, the lost cd-anchor context, the doc URL convention mismatch) versus X's shorter, more general directives.
